key_insight: Introducing an explicit, compact trajectory-level strategy that is sampled and communicated to the agent decouples high-level planning from reactive actions, improving exploration and credit assignment across long-horizon tasks. StraTA makes agentic RL more strategic by turning multi-step intent into a first-class learning signal.
problem_solved: Reactive, step-by-step agent policies struggle with long-horizon decision making because they weaken exploration and make credit assignment across extended trajectories difficult; StraTA addresses this by providing an explicit trajectory-level strategy that guides behavior over many steps.
method: Sample a compact, trajectory-level strategy (an abstract intent or plan) at episode or subtask boundaries.
Condition the low-level policy on the sampled strategy so actions are purposeful and temporally consistent rather than purely reactive.
Train with RL objectives and incentives that reward adherence to useful strategies and improve credit assignment over extended trajectories.
impact: StraTA helps practitioners build agentic LLMs and RL agents that explore more effectively and learn long-range dependencies, making them better suited for complex, multi-step tasks and hierarchical decision problems.
visual_elements: Hierarchy diagram: strategy sampler (top) → conditioned policy (middle) → environment/actions (bottom), showing information flow.

Performance bar/line chart: metric improvements (exploration, success rate, credit assignment) for reactive baseline vs StraTA.
Icon set: strategy/plan icon, policy/agent icon, reward/credit icon to visually link components.
paper_title: StraTA: Incentivizing Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Strategic Trajectory Abstraction
paper_authors: Xiangyuan Xue, Yifan Zhou, Zidong Wang, Shengji Tang, Philip Torr
